hypothesis_evaluation.actionable_consequence: The scaffold-diversity receipt's CORROBORATED_IN_AUDIT_INSTRUMENT verdict, read as an aggregate 'the accepted set is diverse' claim, does not hold at family resolution: the two linear-chain homologous families are literal textbook trivially-inflated-variant series (differ only by a repeated -CH2- or -CH2CH2NH- unit), and the SAME ECFP-r2/2048 instrument the receipt relies on cannot resolve most adjacent members of either family from one another. Any downstream use of the IntDiv_1=0.7681 aggregate to argue the generator avoids near-duplicate proposals must be corrected to disclose that this holds only across families, not within the two homolog families comprising nearly half the accepted set.

hypothesis_evaluation.evidence: F1_polyethyleneamine (n=8, 21.1% of set): IntDiv_1=0.1851 (mean Tanimoto 0.8149), 5/7 adjacent chain-length-neighbor pairs fingerprint-saturated at Tanimoto>=0.99 (TETA-TEPA-PEHA-k6-k7-k8 all pairwise identical). F2_alpha_omega_diamine (n=10, 26.3% of set): IntDiv_1=0.0870 (mean Tanimoto 0.9130), 7/9 adjacent pairs saturated. Both families independently violate the decision rule despite the receipt's headline aggregate IntDiv_1=0.7681 -- the aggregate is driven by cross-family contrast (homolog-bloc-vs-ring mean Tanimoto=0.1054) and conceals near-total indistinguishability within 47.4% of the corpus under the receipt's own instrument.

theory_reference.homologous_series_fingerprint_saturation: Known limitation of finite-radius circular fingerprints on linear repeat-unit chains: once chain length exceeds ~2x the fingerprint radius, added repeat units contribute no new substructure environments beyond those already hashed into the bit vector, so ECFP-r2 similarity between chain homologs saturates toward 1.0 (folding/collision effects in a fixed-width 2048-bit vector reinforce this for the longer members).
